title: Purpose, Tone and Point of View
subject: language

sections.body: Every text has a PURPOSE: to inform, persuade, entertain, instruct or explain. Ask: why was this written?
TONE is the writer's attitude: serious, playful, angry, hopeful, sarcastic. Word choice reveals it: 'a bold plan' vs 'a reckless plan'.
POINT OF VIEW: first person ('I'), second person ('you'), third person ('she', 'they'). A first-person narrator only knows what they see and feel, so they can be unreliable.

quiz.q: 'This reckless plan will waste millions.' The writer's tone is…
hints: Is 'reckless' a positive or negative word?
'This brilliant plan will save millions' would be admiring. What's the opposite feeling?

quiz.q: A story told by 'I' is in which point of view?
hints: Which pronoun does the narrator use about themselves?
'I' and 'we' belong to one point of view.
'She walked home' is third person; 'You walk home' is second person. What's left for 'I'?

quiz.q: 'Step 1: Unplug the printer. Step 2: Open the lid. Step 3: Gently pull out the jammed paper.' What is this text's main purpose?
hints: Ask: why was this written? What does the reader do after reading it?
Numbered steps and command verbs ('Unplug', 'Open', 'pull') are clues.
'Get the new X200, the fastest printer ever!' is written to persuade, because it wants you to buy something.
quiz.explain: Numbered steps and command verbs tell the reader how to do a task, so the purpose is to instruct.
